feedback: Written before this candidate races. Iteration 3 (±0.08 m span, 16 mm, y=0.03 m) cleared the oval and slalom line losses (zero on both) with oval max_error at 0.0608 m, but the s-bend still lost the line once per run (max_error 0.0656 m) and the score fell to 50.65. Iteration 2 showed that moving the row forward to y=0.05 m raised oval max_error to 0.0637 m and gave slalom line losses, so forward is rejected. Iteration 0 used 12 mm footprints and gave a graded signal with a narrower span, but it also lost the line once per run, so the footprint alone is not proven. In the controller I kept kp 8.0 and ki 0.05, so the footprint is the only change this race tests. The next race decides the next step: if the s-bend line loss goes to zero with 12 mm and max_error is near 0.061 m on the oval, keep the geometry fixed and treat controller bias as the remaining limit. If the s-bend still loses the line at 12 mm, move the row back to y=0.01 m rather than forward or wider. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2, reduce mass.
requested_changes: Keep sensor_size at 0.012 m with the ±0.08 m span and y=0.03 m, because the s-bend line loss in iteration 3 is the only failure left and the footprint is the lever. If line_loss_events is still 1 or more on the s-bend, move the row to y=0.01 m with the same seven x positions, not forward, since iteration 2 showed forward raised max_error from 0.0613 to 0.0637 m.

If line losses are zero but max_error stays above 0.06 m on the oval, keep the geometry fixed, because iteration 1 and 3 both sat at about 0.061 m regardless of span. The remaining limit is then controller bias, which the Integrator will address in the controller.
If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2 with the ±0.08 m span (iteration 3 showed 0.158 on the oval), reduce mass from 0.6 to 0.5 kg to cut yaw inertia, keeping sensor positions fixed.
